title: System Administrator (IT)
description:
Server Administration

* Install, configure, and maintain Windows and Linux servers.
* Monitor System health, performance, storage, resource utilization and carry out capacity planning.
* Manage virtualization platforms and virtual machines, where applicable.
* Maintain system uptime and schedule maintenance with minimal disruption to academic and administrative work.

User Account and Access Management

* Create, modify, and deactivate user accounts for staff, faculty, and students.
* Manage Active Directory / directory services, groups, permissions, and password policies.
* Maintain role-based access to systems, shared folders, and applications.

Endpoint and Desktop Management

* Deploy, configure, and support desktops, laptops, and lab computers, including OS imaging and standard software installation.
* Manage patches, updates, and antivirus / endpoint protection across all devices.

Backup, Recovery, and Business Continuity

* Configure and monitor automated on-site and cloud / off-site backups.
* Review backup failures, retention, encryption, and access controls.
* Perform regular restore tests and support disaster recovery planning.

Security and Compliance

* Apply security patches and system hardening in a timely manner.
* Protect institutional data and respond to security incidents affecting servers or endpoints.
* Support audits and ensure compliance with university IT policies and software licensing terms.
* Administer email, collaboration, and productivity platforms (e.g. Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace).

Helpdesk and User Support

* Provide first- and second-line technical support to users.
* Log, track, and resolve incidents and service requests within agreed timelines.
* Escalate complex issues to the IT Head/registrar.

IT Asset Management

* Maintain an up-to-date inventory of hardware, software, and licenses.
* Track warranties, renewals, and asset allocation, repair, and disposal.

Documentation and Reporting

* Maintain system documentation, configuration records, and standard operating procedures.
* Submit periodic IT status reports to the IT Head covering incidents, uptime, backups, and pending actions.

3. Qualifications and Experience

**Requirement**

**Details**

Education

Diploma or bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science or related field

Experience

2–3 years of hands-on system administration experience

Preferred

Experience in a university, school, or multi-branch organization

4. Skills and Competencies

* Strong working knowledge of Windows, Active Directory, and Linux administration.
* Experience with backup solutions, endpoint protection, and patch management tools.
* Good troubleshooting skills and the ability to work independently.
* Clear communication, able to explain technical issues to non-technical staff and management.
* Strong documentation, time management, and service-oriented attitude.

5. Preferred Candidate Profile

A hands-on, dependable administrator who can independently resolve system issues, , support multiple campuses, and communicate clearly with management and end users.

6. Reporting and Employment

Full-time position reporting to the IT Head or Registrar. This is an ongoing, university-wide role.

Pay: ₹200,000.00 - ₹400,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Provident Fund

Work Location: In person
